keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks Huang). The infobox gives no dates and no area; 'Huang is depicted within Chu, east of Sui'. The 45 km disc at Huangchuan is a stand-in. The page dates no territorial change before 648.

region.text: Huang, capital at Huangchuan, Henan ('Capital: Huangchuan'; artifacts unearthed there since 1975)

ledger.note: 704: Huang first appears in the record, refusing Chu's summons. 'Huang and Sui didn't attend a meeting called upon by Chu' (704 BCE); Chu reprimanded Huang and attacked Sui. The page dates no founding ('Their ruling family's surname may have been either Ying or Mi'; an undated Bamboo Annals expedition against the 'Huangyi'), so 704 is the first dated mention, a bridge.

region.text: Huang, capital at Huangchuan, Henan ('Capital: Huangchuan'; artifacts unearthed there since 1975)

ledger.note: 648: Chu extinguishes Huang. The Huang ruler, refusing tribute, said 'It is 900 li from Ying to our domain. How can they harm us?'; Chu then invaded and 'extinguished Huang'. The page says nothing of the land afterwards (the chu dossier names the counterpart 'the State of Huang').

region.text: Huang, capital at Huangchuan, Henan ('Capital: Huangchuan'; artifacts unearthed there since 1975)

ledger.note: 648: the state of Huang ends in Chu's invasion; the page's last dated event.

wars.name: Chu attack on Huang at Jiling

zones.text: Huang, capital at Huangchuan, Henan ('Capital: Huangchuan'; artifacts unearthed there since 1975)

wars.outcome: In 675 BC 'the King of Chu attacked Huang at Jiling (踖陵) and defeated them'; Huang survived, and by 658 had made a covenant with Qi and Song.
wars.note: The page does not say that Huang became a Chu vassal in 675, so no vassal event is written.

wars.name: Chu conquest of Huang

zones.text: Huang, capital at Huangchuan, Henan ('Capital: Huangchuan'; artifacts unearthed there since 1975)

wars.outcome: Huang refused tribute and was invaded and extinguished by Chu in 648 BC.
wars.note: The Qi-sponsored covenant of 658 with Song, Jiang and Qi and the joint attack on Chen in 656 ('Jiang, Huang, and Lu jointly attacked Chen on Qi's behalf') are on the page; they moved no border.

certainty.note: No Huang boundary is on the page; soft throughout.

notes: Pages opened (2 of 1-2): Huang (state), List of Zhou dynasty states. Wikidata id left null (unreachable). START -704 is the first dated mention, a bridge (confidence 1): the page gives no founding date; the 'List of Zhou dynasty states' (second page opened) gives the table row 'Huang (黃國, Henan): Shang Era-648 BCE, conquered by Chu 648 BCE, Huangchuan County, Henan Province', which confirms the end year and the site but gives no date for the Shang-era start. REGION: Huangchuan is not in the gazetteer (listed under gazetteer_names_needed); the disc is by coordinates. The chu dossier (ea-01-a) draws Huang as Xinyang 80 km, which leaves Huangchuan about 10 km outside; the dossiers should share one region. This is the Huang of Henan; a second Huang on the Fen River in Shanxi (annexed by Jin) is a different state. AREA: none on the page. The page lists no rulers (a ding names a ruler Meng).
